modern: From my tutor, to be neither of the Green nor of the Blue party at the games in the Circus, nor a supporter of either the Parmularius or the Scutarius at the gladiators’ fights; from him too I learned to endure hard work, and to want little, and to work with my own hands, and not to meddle in other people’s affairs, and not to be ready to listen to slander.

explained.summary:
Marcus credits his tutor with a handful of habits that keep you steady: don’t throw yourself into tribal rivalries, put up with hard work, want less, do things yourself, stay out of other people’s business, and don’t lend your ear to gossip.

The Greens and Blues were the rival chariot-racing teams, with fans as fierce as any today. The point isn’t that sport is bad, but that picking a side and getting worked up over it is a cheap way to lose your calm.
explained.today: The modern Greens and Blues are the football rivalry, the online pile-on or the office faction you’re invited to join. Wanting little might mean not upgrading the phone that works fine; minding your own business might mean not forwarding the screenshot in the group chat.
